altReasons: Scoring margin: Brewers favored (+214 run diff vs Padres +41, a 173-run gap)
Rest: Padres favored (Brewers used 5 relievers across 5 innings in Game 1, including a 4-out save from closer Trevor Megill, leaving Milwaukee's bullpen more taxed entering Game 2)
Weather/Venue: Brewers favored (American Family Field's closed roof already produced one Game 1 'home-field break' when a Ty France fly ball struck a roof beam and was caught for an out)
Market: Padres favored (reverse line movement -- Padres drawing roughly 51% of moneyline money despite only ~40% of bets, with the line moving from +117 to +123 on San Diego)
Matchup splits: Brewers favored (Milwaukee's .759 team OPS vs RHP comfortably outpaces San Diego's .719 vs RHP, and both starters -- King and Henderson -- throw right-handed)
Scoring margin: Dodgers favored (+201 run diff vs Braves +116, an 85-run gap)

Injuries/Lineup: Braves favored (Lane Thomas returns to Atlanta's lineup for the first time since a Sept. 7 rib/intercostal strain, while Dodgers DH Shohei Ohtani is playing through lingering knee/biceps/neck issues he says he'll have to 'manage' through the postseason)
Form: Braves favored (Atlanta went 6-4 over its final 10 regular-season games vs. Los Angeles' 5-5)
Matchup splits: Dodgers favored (Braves hit just .696 team OPS vs LHP this season, and tonight's Dodgers starter Blake Snell throws left-handed)
games.note: NLDS Game 2 (Dodgers lead series 1-0). Braves Game 2 starter was unconfirmed as of generation time (Sunday morning) -- multiple pregame sources had 'all signs point to Chris Sale', with Grant Holmes/JR Ritchie as fallback options; pitcher stats below use Sale.
